source.title: Design, Fabrication, and In-Flight Demonstration of a 24S NCM Battery System for an eVTOL Aircraft

ground_test_pack.dcir_method: estimated_from_initial_voltage_drop_between_different_discharge_rate_tests; not a standard same-soc pulse measurement

ground_test_conditions.caution: The 10.68C test ran for 4 min 9 s and reduced usable capacity to 74.2% of the 1C reference. It is not a demonstrated continuous-service operating point.

flight_demonstration.estimated_load_basis: indirect voltage-based and propulsion-bench estimates for a 140 kg test mass
limitations: The in-flight current was not directly measured synchronously with pack voltage.
Pack and cell temperatures were not measured during flight.
The flight session used about 5 C ambient and 2-3 m/s wind, not a representative hot/high/windy operational envelope.
Pack-to-pack current sharing could not be inferred from parallel pack voltages.
The study describes this as an initial in-flight demonstration, not full UAM-envelope validation.

best_use: open published eVTOL pack/system specific-energy reference
thermal and voltage-sag model calibration candidate
must_not_be_used_as: a direct passenger aircraft range claim
a validated hot-day or end-of-life battery capability
proof that 10.68C is a sustainable continuous operating rate
benchmark_interpretation.claim_ceiling: Published pack-level ground-test and initial in-flight demonstrator evidence with stated limitations; no type certification or representative operational-envelope validation is established.
